operatorChanges: Configure the requested model explicitly and require the durable model receipt to match it.
Use the active access-only Eva2 lease and identity instead of the old full-login source.
Allow the existing hash-bound development scan only in fresh local-candidate mode; it is explicitly not release authority.
Verify committed reply replay and a new recall question after joint restart.

unitTestIncident.finding: Two existing tests assumed different real runner UIDs. Running the suite as root caused the negative receipt-owner test to start a unique old-image disposable stack unintentionally.
unitTestIncident.stoppedAt: dashboard-authority-install: old default image lacked eva.operations.initialize_dashboard_authority; no foreground model call occurred.
unitTestIncident.liveImpact: No live data cloned, no production container modified. All temporary containers, network, volumes and credential staging were removed; live readiness stayed HTTP 200.
unitTestIncident.repair: The unsafe-parent test now uses an explicitly unsafe mode independent of UID and forbids subprocess/network calls. The final-receipt test isolates destination validation and also forbids subprocesses.
unitTestIncident.after: All 61 focused tests passed as the ordinary user (1.08 s) and as root (0.74 s); Ruff and component catalog passed.

retention.cleanupAfter: Independent acceptance of the replacement conversation image. Temporary runtime databases and credentials are already removed.

independentReview.decision: GO for accuracy of this development proof only; CO-002 remains open.
independentReview.verified: Retained fresh-stack and invocation hashes, candidate/source/model bindings, 4440 foreground tokens, same-conversation restart/replay and stated nonclaims.

nonclaims: No real Telegram message, external tool effect, production-data migration or live promotion was performed.
This is a development runtime proof, not RB-007, RB-008 release acceptance, complete release approval or human acceptance.
No general conversation-quality or competitor-superiority claim follows from exact-word recall.
